header.service: DEMO — UC San Diego Athletics Fan & Revenue Lifecycle
header.scope: First contact with Triton athletics → Renewal, lapse, or a first Triton Athletic Fund gift
header.lead: A. Practice Lead, Director of AI Strategy

entries.where: Stage 2 (First purchase); cycle-wide; H-02, H-04, H-06
entries.whatsWrong: There is no shared identifier across the ticketing platform, the email platform, the Athletics donor records, and the central Advancement CRM, so one person exists as four unlinked records.
entries.whoFeels: Fans and donors; everyone who has to answer a question about a person
entries.evidence: INT-5: "The two systems have no shared identifier, so matching a season-ticket holder to a donor record is a name-and-address exercise"; INT-1: "It's all one thing to me — it's Triton basketball — but it clearly isn't one thing on their end"
entries.notes: The root condition beneath most of this register. Everything downstream is an attempt to work around it by hand.

entries.whatsWrong: Audience lists are exported from ticketing and re-uploaded to the email platform by hand for every campaign, so targeting runs on data that is already about a week old.
entries.whoFeels: Marketing staff; fans who get offers for games they already bought
entries.evidence: INT-2: "every campaign starts with me exporting a file and re-uploading it — by the time it's in my hands it's a week old"; INT-1: "some of them were for games I'd already bought tickets to"
entries.notes: The staleness is what makes the targeting decision worse than the marketer's own judgment would be.

entries.whatsWrong: Attendance is recorded as a scan against a barcode and returned as a gate count, so the unit cannot say, account by account, who was in the building or who came back.
entries.whoFeels: Marketing, ticket operations, and the Fund — everyone downstream of attendance
entries.evidence: INT-3: "We do not know, account by account, who was in the building"; INT-2: "Scans come back to me as a gate count, not as accounts"
entries.notes: The strongest signal of interest in the whole lifecycle is collected at the door and then discarded.

entries.whatsWrong: Post-event follow-up goes to the account that bought the tickets rather than to the person who attended on a transferred ticket, so an interested attendee is never contacted.
entries.whoFeels: Guests attending on transferred tickets; the buyer, who gets everything twice
entries.evidence: INT-1: "I got the 'thanks for coming' email both times, my friend never got anything"; INT-3: "if the ticket was transferred the barcode isn't the buyer anymore"
entries.notes: A silent leak: the fan who might convert is invisible to the system that would ask them.

entries.where: Stage 5 (Renewal or a first gift); H-04
entries.whatsWrong: The season-ticket holder file reaches the Triton Athletic Fund as a monthly email export, so the Fund solicits from a picture that is weeks out of date.
entries.whoFeels: The Fund; recent joiners who are missed and recent lapses who are asked anyway
entries.evidence: INT-4: "the season-ticket holder file, which reaches me as a monthly export" — "I'm always soliciting off a picture that's a few weeks old"; INT-3: "I pull it and email it over, usually once a month"
entries.notes: Directly degrades the highest-judgment decision in the map.

entries.where: Stage 5 (Renewal or a first gift); H-06; D-05
entries.whatsWrong: A fan already assigned to a central Advancement officer can be solicited by Athletics without either side knowing, because clearance is requested case by case and often after the letter has gone out.
entries.whoFeels: Donors who give to both; gift officers on both sides
entries.evidence: INT-4: "the ask usually happens after I've already sent the letter"; INT-5: "I find out about an ask when the gift lands" and "we've had a case where two officers were cultivating the same household for the same year"
entries.notes: The clearest cross-unit failure in the map, and the one the group has not yet settled.

entries.where: Stage 5 (Renewal or a first gift); H-05
entries.whatsWrong: Gift processing and receipting for Fund gifts routes through central Advancement on a batch cycle, so acknowledgment lags the gift by around six weeks.
entries.whoFeels: First-time donors; the Fund director fielding the calls
entries.evidence: INT-1: "the receipt took about six weeks to show up"; INT-4: "I've had donors call me about a receipt I can't produce"
entries.notes: Falls hardest on first-time donors, whose only evidence that the gift landed is the receipt.

entries.whatsWrong: Renewal invoices and annual-fund asks land in the same window because the two teams do not share a solicitation calendar, so the fan receives two asks from what they experience as one institution.
entries.whoFeels: Season-ticket holders; both teams, when the response is worse than either expected
entries.evidence: INT-1: "which came about four days after the renewal invoice" — "you just asked me for money"; INT-2: "Nobody tells me when the Fund is about to mail the same people I'm mailing"
entries.notes: The moment the institution's internal structure becomes visible to the person it serves.

entries.whatsWrong: Win-back runs manually from a spreadsheet after the season and is worked in order until staff time runs out, so whether a lapsed buyer is contacted depends on capacity rather than on who they were.
entries.whoFeels: Lapsed buyers who are never contacted; marketing staff
entries.evidence: INT-2: "whether it happens at all depends on whether I have a student worker that month"
entries.notes: Compounds the fact that lapse is discovered a season late in the first place.

clusters.name: One relationship, many records
clusters.sharedRoot: Nothing links the person across systems, and the one moment that proves interest — walking through the gate — is recorded against a barcode rather than an account. The institution ends up holding fragments of a relationship it cannot reassemble.

clusters.name: Hand-worked lists
clusters.sharedRoot: Because no system talks to the next one, both targeting and win-back run off exported files worked by hand, so the quality of the outreach tracks staff time and file age rather than the marketer's judgment.

clusters.name: The buyer-to-donor boundary
clusters.sharedRoot: At the point where a ticket buyer becomes a donor, the work changes both systems and units at once. A monthly file, a clearance request made after the fact, and a central batch receipt cycle all sit on the same seam.

clusters.name: Two asks, one institution
clusters.sharedRoot: Outreach is addressed to records rather than to people: the buyer of record gets everything, the person who actually attended gets nothing, and two teams working the same household in the same week cannot see each other.

data.honestAccount:
DEMO — the fan experience in this lifecycle is good right up until the institution has to remember who someone is. Buying works, game day works, and the fan's own account of the evening is the strongest thing in the map. What breaks is continuity: the same person exists as a ticket account, an email contact, a barcode, and two donor records, and the only moment that proves genuine interest — walking through the gate — is captured as a count and thrown away. Everything downstream is an attempt to reconstruct by hand what was never linked: a monthly file emailed to the Fund, a segment list a week out of date, a win-back spreadsheet worked as far as staff time allows.

The heaviest friction sits exactly where the brief expected it, at the handoff from ticket buyer to donor, because that is the one point where the systems and the units change at the same time. A clearance request that arrives after the letter has gone out is not a process failure so much as a structural one: neither side can see the other's record of the same person.

Where this map is thin: it rests on one fan's account rather than several, so the experience side of stages 4 and 6 is documented from a single voice. Nothing here proposes a fix, and nothing here should be read as an argument for scoring fans or donors — the register records that the Fund's selection decision runs on human judgment today, and that the unit asked for care before that changes.
